dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Nam, your email is clear, but some of your words are too informal.
dialogue.reading: ˈnɑːm, jʊr ˈiːmeɪl ɪz ˈklɪr, bʌt sʌm əv jʊr ˈwɜːrdz ər ˈtuː ɪnˈfɔːrməl.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Here you wrote, "I bought a three-night stay." In a formal email, write, "I purchased a three-night stay."
dialogue.reading: ˈhɪr juː ˈroʊt, aɪ ˈbɔːt ə ˌθriː ˌnaɪt ˈsteɪ. ɪn ə ˈfɔːrməl ˈiːmeɪl, ˈraɪt, aɪ ˈpɜːrtʃəst ə ˌθriː ˌnaɪt ˈsteɪ.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: "I got your email" should be "I received your email." And don't write, "Can you help me?" Write, "Could you assist me?"
dialogue.reading: aɪ ˈɡɑːt jʊr ˈiːmeɪl ʃʊd bi aɪ rɪˈsiːvd jʊr ˈiːmeɪl. ənd ˈdoʊnt ˈraɪt, kən juː ˈhɛlp miː? ˈraɪt, kʊd juː əˈsɪst miː?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: I also wrote, "Please tell me what you decide."
dialogue.reading: aɪ ˈɔːlsoʊ ˈroʊt, ˈpliːz ˈtɛl miː ˈwʌt juː dɪˈsaɪd.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Try, "Please inform me of your decision." That's more formal.
dialogue.reading: ˈtraɪ, ˈpliːz ɪnˈfɔːrm miː əv jʊr dɪˈsɪʒən. ðæts ˈmɔːr ˈfɔːrməl.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: And here: "The hotel didn't have enough staff."
dialogue.reading: ənd ˈhɪr: ðə hoʊˈtɛl ˈdɪdənt ˈhæv ɪˈnʌf ˈstæf.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: In formal writing, "The hotel did not have sufficient staff." Notice: "did not," not "didn't."
dialogue.reading: ɪn ˈfɔːrməl ˈraɪtɪŋ, ðə hoʊˈtɛl dɪd ˈnɑːt ˈhæv səˈfɪʃənt ˈstæf. ˈnoʊtɪs: ˈdɪd ˈnɑːt, ˈnɑːt ˈdɪdənt.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: What about "I need a copy of the invoice"?
dialogue.reading: ˈwʌt əˈbaʊt aɪ ˈniːd ə ˈkɑːpi əv ði ˈɪnvɔɪs?

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: You could write, "I require a copy of the invoice." But don't use too many formal words. Keep it clear.
dialogue.reading: juː kʊd ˈraɪt, aɪ rɪˈkwaɪər ə ˈkɑːpi əv ði ˈɪnvɔɪs. bʌt ˈdoʊnt ˈjuːz ˈtuː ˈmɛni ˈfɔːrməl ˈwɜːrdz. ˈkiːp ɪt ˈklɪr.
